paragraphs: Yesh meqomot nohagim dehakkohanim matchilin tebat "yebarekka" meatzman, veen hachazzan miqra otam ella mittebat "Adonai veyishmereka" veelak, vezo hassebara shekkatab maran za"l beshulchano hattahor, ak yesh omerim shetztzarik hachazzan lehaqrot otam gam tebat "yebarekka" mishshum diktib "emor lahem" veyesh qepida baddabar, abal hacholeqim sebira lehu deen qepida im lo amar lahem tebat "yebarekka", veal pi hassod yesh qepida bazeh lomar lahem gam tebat "yebarekka", vkm"sh rabbenu bechayye za"l beparashat nasa tamo shel dabar shetztzarik lehaqrot gam "yebarekka" yeuyyan sham, veken nohagim hachasidim bebet el ykb"tz birushalim tibbaneh vetikkonen, vehinneh poh irenu bagdad y" haya hamminhag mizzeman qadmon kemo shekkatab maran za"l deen hachazzan miqra tebat "yebarekka", ak qodem kamma shanim tehillot lael yitbarek sheazarani laasot hamminhag bekol batte kenesiyyot shebbeirenu sheyyihyeh hachazzan miqra tebat "yebarekka" gam ken veken rauy lehorot bekol atar vaatar, veahane lan tuba minhag zeh sheal yede ken lo yobdu hatztzibbur amen sheachar birkat "yisrael beahaba" ki mittechilla haya darkam shel kohanim lemaher lomar "yebarekka" tekep umiyyad achar tebat "beahaba" bemeshek echad, veal yede ken lo haya epshar laanot amen:

clarification.explanation: Regarding Birkat Kohanim (the Priestly Blessing), customs differ as to how it begins. Some practice that the kohanim open the word "yevarechecha" on their own, and the chazzan calls out to them only from the words "Hashem veyishmerecha" onward - and this is the position of Maran in the Shulchan Aruch. But some say that the chazzan must call out to the kohanim the word "yevarechecha" as well, as it is said "say to them," and according to the esoteric tradition one must be careful to call out "yevarechecha" to them as well. In Baghdad the custom from earlier times followed Maran's view that the chazzan does not call out "yevarechecha," but our teacher [the Ben Ish Chai] changed the custom in all the synagogues of the city so that the chazzan would call out "yevarechecha" as well, and so it is fitting to instruct everywhere. This custom brings great benefit, for through it the congregation does not lose out on answering "amen" after the blessing "Yisrael be'ahavah," since previously the kohanim would hurry to say "yevarechecha" immediately after "be'ahavah" in a single breath, leaving the congregation no time to answer amen.
takeaways: Our teacher instituted that the chazzan calls out to the kohanim the word "yevarechecha" as well, and so it is fitting everywhere.
The benefit: the congregation has time to answer amen after the blessing "Yisrael be'ahavah."

paragraphs: Im en kohanim laasot nesiut kappayim vehazzeman rauy linsiut kappayim - az hashlicha tzibbur omer "barekenu bibraka veku'" kannizkar bassiddurim, veen hatztzibbur onim amen achar happesuqim, ella omerim "ken yihyeh ratzon", achar kol pasuq, vekatab bechesed lealpayim: minhag vatiqin lomar achar pasuq rishon "ken yehi ratzon bizkut abraham", veachar pasuq sheni "ken yehi ratzon bizkut yitzchaq", veachar pasuq shelishi "ken yehi ratzon bizkut yaaqob ubizkut mosheh veaharon veyosep vedavid":

clarification.explanation: If there are no kohanim for the raising of hands, and the time is appropriate for it, the prayer leader says "Bless us with the blessing," etc. (in the wording found in the prayer books), and the congregation does not answer "amen" after the verses, but says "May it be [His] will" after each verse. Chesed LeAlafim writes that the custom of the vatikin is to say after the first verse "May it be [His] will, in the merit of Abraham," after the second "in the merit of Isaac," and after the third "in the merit of Jacob, and in the merit of Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David."
takeaways: When there are no kohanim, the prayer leader says "Bless us with the blessing," and the congregation answers "May it be [His] will" after each verse (not "amen").
The custom of the vatikin: "May it be [His] will, in the merit of Abraham/Isaac/Jacob and Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David" after the verses.

paragraphs: Kesheomer hashlicha tzibbur "yebarekka" - yihyeh letzad hahekol, "veyishmereka" - letzad yamin, "yaer Adonai panayv" - kelappe hahekol, "eleka vichunnak" - letzad semol; ken katab bechesed lealpayim, ak harab beno sham katab beshem "appe zutere" shehebi meiggerot harab mosheh zekuta za"l: "yebarekka" - letzad yamin shello, "yaer" - letzad semol, "yissa" - letzad panayv vekatab sham shekken hamminhag pashut beir haqqodesh yerushalayim tibbaneh vetikkonen veken nohagim baqqahal chasidim bebet el ykb"tz y", veshaalti meet yedidenu harab haggaon morenu harab eliyyahu minni nr"v sheyyodieni minhag hachasidim bebet el ykb"tz bedabar zeh, vekatab li veza"l: "moda lebenah demah shekkatab "appe zutere" beshem iggerot harab mosheh zekuta za"l en reaya, vaani noheg kilshon hazzohar ukemo shekkatab "chesed laalapim", velo kemo shehiggihha harab beno, uminhag bet el ykb"tz kemo sheani oseh, veayyen "tepillat kol peh" dap p' ammud g veayyen "kap hachayyim" siman tv ot z shettebat "yebarekka veku'" - letzad hahekol, "veyishmereka" - letzad yamin, "yaer" - letzad hahekol, "eleka veyachenka"- letzad semol, "yissa" - leneged hahekol, veqav haemtzai - shehu gupo; ad kan leshono nr"v:

clarification.explanation: To which side should the prayer leader turn during Birkat Kohanim? Opinions differ: According to Chesed LeAlafim - "yevarechecha" faces toward the Ark, "veyishmerecha" toward the right, "ya'er Hashem panav" toward the Ark, "eilecha vichunecha" toward the left. But his son quoted in the name of "Apei Zutrei" (from the letters of the Ramaz, of blessed memory): "yevarechecha" to his right, "ya'er" to his left, "yisa" toward his face - and wrote that this is the custom in Jerusalem and in Beit El. The Ben Ish Chai asked Rabbi Eliyahu Mani, may his light shine, [about this], and he replied that there is no proof for the words of "Apei Zutrei," and that he practices according to the language of the Zohar and as Chesed LeAlafim wrote (and not as the son's emendation), and so is the custom of Beit El. See also Kaf HaChaim: "yevarechecha" toward the Ark, "veyishmerecha" to the right, "ya'er" toward the Ark, "eilecha vichunecha" to the left, "yisa" opposite the Ark, and the middle line - opposite his own body.
takeaways: The direction the prayer leader faces during Birkat Kohanim - a dispute between Chesed LeAlafim (following the language of the Zohar) and his son's emendation (in the name of the Ramaz).

In practice, following the language of the Zohar/Kaf HaChaim: "yevarechecha"/"ya'er"/"yisa" toward the Ark, "veyishmerecha" to the right, "eilecha vichunecha" to the left (and the middle facing his own body) - and so is the custom of Beit El.

paragraphs: Kol kohen sheen bo echad mehaddebarim hamakkebim, im eno oleh laddukan bittel mitzvat aseh, vechashub keober bishlosha aseh im haya bebet hakkeneset beshaa sheqqara hachazzan "kohanim", o im ameru lo beperush laalot o littol yadayv, vekol kohen hammebarek mitbarek mippi elyon, utehillot lael poh irenu bagdad y" nizharim laasot nesiut kappayim bekol yom, veken rauy linhog bekol haqqehillot deal yede birkat kohanim yimmashek shepa laelyonim velattachtonim, veyesh bah raze derazin ashre ayin raata:

clarification.explanation: Any kohen who has no disqualifying factor preventing him from raising his hands, and who does not go up to the duchan, has nullified a positive commandment. And if he was in the synagogue at the time the chazzan called "Kohanim," or was explicitly told to go up or to wash his hands, he is considered to have transgressed three positive commandments. Every kohen who blesses is blessed from Heaven. In Baghdad they were careful to raise hands every day, and so it is fitting to practice in all congregations, for through Birkat Kohanim abundance is drawn down to the upper and lower worlds, and it contains deep secrets.
takeaways: A kohen who is fit to bless and refrains has nullified a positive commandment.
It is fitting to raise hands every day, as is the custom of Baghdad, since Birkat Kohanim draws down abundance.

paragraphs: Meqom amidat hakkohanim lebarek hu al haitztabba sheetzel kotel hammaarab hammitpallelim kenegdo, ki mashmaut "dukan" rotzeh lomar itztabba, vehammitrashshel bazeh shello laalot al haddukan laamod sham, ella omed beqarqa hahekol, hare zeh meshanneh middibre chaza"l, ki lo al chinnam ameru chaza"l laalot hakkohanim al haddukan, upoh irenu y" haya minhagam laamod hakkohanim beqarqa hahekol ulebarek birkat kohanim veenam omedim al haitztabba shebbesop hahekol, utehillot lael asiti hamminhag sheyyaalu veyaamdu al haitztabba shebbesop hahekol vesham yebareku, veken rauy ledaqdeq bazeh bekol atar vaatar:

clarification.explanation: The place where the kohanim stand to bless is on the platform (a raised step) next to the wall which the congregation faces in prayer, for this is the meaning of "duchan." A kohen who is lax and does not go up onto the duchan, remaining on the floor of the sanctuary, deviates from the words of the Sages who required going up specifically onto the duchan. In Baghdad the kohanim used to stand on the floor of the sanctuary, and our teacher instituted that they go up and stand on the platform at the rear of the sanctuary and bless there, and so it is fitting to be scrupulous about this everywhere.
takeaways: The kohanim must go up and stand on the duchan (the raised platform), not on the floor.
Our teacher instituted this correction in Baghdad, and so it is fitting everywhere.

paragraphs: Lo yaalu hakkohanim laddukan beminalim vaapillu hem shel beged kegon ellu shellobeshim beyom hakkippurim, veyesh machmirim bebatte shoqayim im hem shel or:

clarification.explanation: The kohanim shall not go up to the duchan while wearing shoes, even shoes made of cloth, such as those worn on Yom Kippur. And some are stringent even regarding light house-slippers, if they are made of leather.
takeaways: One may not go up to the duchan wearing shoes, even if they are made of cloth.
Some are stringent even regarding light cloth slippers with a leather sole.

paragraphs: Ap al pi shennatelu hakkohanim yedehem shacharit, chozerim venotelim qodem birkat kohanim, netila gemura ad happereq shehu chibbur hayyad vehazzeroa, vehallevi yotzeq mayim al yedehem, veqodem laken yittol hallevi et yadayv, veim en sham levi yotzeq lahem habbekor meim shehu peter rechem, veim en sham bekor yittelu beatzmam velo al yede yisrael, veyesh omerim sheim hallevi hu talmid chakam eno rashshay latzuq mayim al yede hakkohanim apillu im miqtzatam talmide chakamim umiqtzatam amme haaretz, vekol shekken im kullam amme haaretz vechayyab mita bide shamayim im hetziq mayim al yad kohen am haaretz, veap sheyyesh mattirin bazeh- lemichash bae vesheb veal taaseh adip, vaapillu im en sham levi ella hu:

clarification.explanation: Even though the kohanim washed their hands in the morning, they wash again before Birkat Kohanim - a complete washing up to the joint (where the hand meets the forearm). The Levite pours water on their hands, and beforehand the Levite washes his own hands. If there is no Levite, a firstborn son (from his mother's womb) pours for them; and if there is no firstborn, they wash by themselves and not through an Israelite. Some say that if the Levite is a Torah scholar, he may not pour for an unlearned kohen, and there is great stringency in this matter. And since there is a dispute about it, it is preferable to refrain (sit and do not act), even when there is no other Levite available.
takeaways: The kohanim wash their hands again before the blessing, up to the forearm joint, and the Levite pours for them.
Order of priority for who pours: a Levite; if none, a firstborn; and if neither, the kohanim themselves.

paragraphs: Kol kohen yere shamayim yishmor yadayv mishsheat netilato shacharit shello liga bimqomot hamkussim begupo, sheim naga yesh sapeq shetztzarik lachazor ulebarek keshennotel yadayv lebirkat kohanim, veyesh omerim debaenan mayim tehorim shello nishtannu mibberiyyatan, ubaenan name koach gabra kedin netilat yadayim, veda shetztzarik sheyyihyeh tekep lintila beraka, al ken yizzaher heka deepshar lo shello yishheh kede hilluk k"b amma ben netila lebirkat kohanim:

clarification.explanation: Every God-fearing kohen should guard his hands from the time of his morning washing, so as not to touch the covered parts of his body, for if he touched them there is a doubt whether he must wash and bless again before Birkat Kohanim. Some say pure water is required, which has not changed in appearance, and human effort in the pouring, as in the law of washing hands [before bread]. And the blessing must be adjacent to the washing; therefore, when possible, he should be careful not to delay between the washing and Birkat Kohanim more than the time it takes to walk twenty-two amot.
takeaways: A kohen should guard his hands from touching covered body parts after the morning washing.
The blessing must be adjacent to the washing, without a delay of more than twenty-two amot's walk.

paragraphs: Kesheyyatchil shelicha tzibbur "retzeh"- kol kohen shebbebet hakkeneset yaaqor mimmeqomo laalot laddukan, vaapillu kohen shehu belav haki omed bahekol shennose bo kappayv im kol zeh tzarik laaqor raglayv b"retzeh", veim lo aqar raglayv qodem shessiyyem shelicha tzibbur "retzeh" lo yaaleh laddukan, veim aqar raglayv achar shessiyyem shelicha tzibbur "retzeh", apillu im ala yered, vaaqira mibbeto kede labo lebet hakkeneset la chashiba aqira leinyan birkat kohanim, velaken im higgia lebet hakkeneset achar shessiyyem shelicha tzibbur "retzeh" lo yaaleh laddukan, raq im hayeta haaqira mibbeto addata dehaki laalot laddukan, az yukal laalot apillu im higgia lebet hakkeneset achar shessiyyem shelicha tzibbur "retzeh", vekatabti bitshuba besipre haq' "rab pealim" desiyyum "ratza" hu kesheamar "hammachazir shekinato letziyyon", ki ad kan niqret birkat aboda, abal min "modim veku'" zo hi birkat hodaa:

clarification.explanation: When the chazzan begins the blessing "Retzeh," every kohen in the synagogue must uproot his feet from his place to go up to the duchan, even a kohen who is already standing in the sanctuary. If he did not uproot his feet before the chazzan finished "Retzeh," he may not go up; and if he uprooted them after the chazzan finished "Retzeh," even if he went up he must come down. Uprooting one's feet from home to come to the synagogue is not considered an uprooting for this purpose, so one who arrives at the synagogue after the chazzan finished "Retzeh" may not go up - unless he left his house with the intention of going up to the duchan. And the conclusion of "Retzeh" is at the words "HaMachazir Shechinato LeTziyon," up to which point it is the blessing of Divine service.
takeaways: The kohen must uproot his feet to go up at the time of "Retzeh," before the chazzan finishes it.
The conclusion of "Retzeh" is at "HaMachazir Shechinato LeTziyon"; one who is late may not go up.

paragraphs: Tzibbur shehayu mitpallelin vehaya bahem shemona yisreelim ushelosha kohanim, veyesh shenayim meellu hashshelosha kohanim en rotzim laasot nesiut kappayim mippene sibba, verotzim latzet chutz lebet hakkeneset veim yetzeu hashshenayim lo yishshaer bebet hakkeneset ella tisha shehem shemona yisreelim veechad kohen ketzad yaasu, heeleti bitshuba besipre haq' "rab pealim" besiyyata dishmayya: tzarik sheyyetzeu qodem sheyyatchil shelicha tzibbur "retzeh", veyishshaaru bachutz ad sheyyachtom shelicha tzibbur "hammachazir shekinato letziyyon", ukesheyyatchil bebirkat modim yikkanesu lebet hakkeneset kede lehashlim hamminyan, veyaaseh hakkohen hannishar bebet hakkeneset sheaqar raglayv b"retzeh" nesiut kappayim lebaddo, vehashshenayim en nosein kappehem kevan shenniknesu achar birkat "modim" velo aqeru raglehem b"retzeh", umah shekkatab morenu harab iserelin za"l vehubeu debarayv beshulchan aruk siman qkch dekohanim hayyotzeim nahagu silsul shello likkanes ella ad sheyyigmeru hakkohanim shebbebet hakkeneset et birkat kohanim, kede shello yomru alehem shehem pegumim, zeh ayre beheka dehatztzibbur asher bebet hakkeneset en tzerikim lahem lehashlim hamminyan, lekak al tzad hayyoter tob nahagu besilsul zeh, abal bikhay gavna ditzrikim lahem lehashlim hamminyan sheim lo yikkanesu qodem habberaka titbattel mitzvat nesiut kappayim, en mebattelin nesiut kappayim min hatztzibbur bishbil silsul zeh shennahagu hakkohanim, mihu bikhay gavna vadday en hsh"tz qore "kohanim":

clarification.explanation: The case: a congregation praying that includes eight Israelites and three kohanim, and two of the kohanim do not wish to raise their hands and wish to leave, and if they leave no minyan will remain. What should they do? They should leave before the chazzan begins "Retzeh," and remain outside until the chazzan concludes "HaMachazir Shechinato LeTziyon," and when he begins "Modim" they should enter to complete the minyan. The kohen who remained and uprooted his feet at "Retzeh" raises his hands alone, and the two others do not raise theirs, since they entered after "Modim" and did not uproot their feet at "Retzeh." And since they are needed to complete the minyan, the raising of hands is not nullified because of them - except that in such a case the chazzan does not call out "Kohanim."
takeaways: Kohanim who will not raise their hands should leave before "Retzeh" and return at "Modim" to complete the minyan.
The kohen who remained blesses alone, and the chazzan does not call out "Kohanim."

paragraphs: Im hitchil shelicha tzibbur tepillat hachazara baasara, veyatzeu mehem qodem birkat kohanim, shello nishar asara - yomar hashlicha tzibbur "eloqenu veallaqe abotenu barekenu babberaka hammeshulleshet" dibraka zo shayeka litpilla vekevan dehitchil baasara gomer beraka zo gam ken, ukemo shekkatab "olat tamid" v"sheyare keneset haggedola" v"eliyya rabba" veken heeleti besiata dishmayya besipre haq' "rab pealim":

clarification.explanation: If the chazzan began the repetition of the prayer with ten present, and afterward people left so that ten no longer remained before Birkat Kohanim, the chazzan shall say "Our God and God of our fathers, bless us with the three-fold blessing," for this blessing belongs to the prayer itself, and since he began with ten, he completes this blessing as well.
takeaways: The chazzan began the repetition with ten, and the minyan diminished before Birkat Kohanim.
He completes it and says "bless us with the three-fold blessing," since it is part of the prayer.

paragraphs: Kesheoqer hakkohen raglayv lissa kappayv yomar "leshem yichud qudesha berik hu ushekinetteh veku' hinneh anoki mukan umezumman leqayyem mitzvat aseh lebarek et yisrael birkat kohanim binsiut kappayim, laasot nachat rucha leyotzerenu ulehamshik shepa uberaka lekol haolamot veku'". ukesheomedim hakkohanim al haddukan leachar sheanu "modim derabbanan", omerim "yehi ratzon millepaneka eloqenu veallaqe abotenu shettihyeh beraka zo shetztzivvitanu lebarek et ammeka yisrael beraka shelema velo yihyeh bah mikshol veaon meatta vead olam", umearikan bitpilla zo ad sheyyesayyem hsh"tz "uleka naeh lehodot", kede shettihyeh aniyyat amen shel haqqahal al zeh veal zeh:

clarification.explanation: When the kohen uproots his feet to raise his hands, he says a short "leshem yichud" formula, [stating] that he is ready and prepared to fulfill the commandment of Birkat Kohanim through the raising of hands, to bring satisfaction to his Creator and to draw down abundance and blessing to all the worlds. And when the kohanim stand on the duchan, after answering "Modim DeRabbanan," they recite a request that this blessing be a complete blessing without stumbling or iniquity, and they prolong this request until the chazzan concludes "U'lecha na'eh lehodot," so that the congregation's amen will rise upon both the chazzan's blessing and their own request.
takeaways: The kohen recites "leshem yichud" as he uproots his feet, along with a request that the blessing be complete.
He prolongs the request until "U'lecha na'eh lehodot," so that the amen applies to both.

paragraphs: La baenan linsiut kappayim maqom sheyyesh bo seper tora, ella bekol maqom shemmitpallelim yesh nesiut kappayim, ukesheolim laddukan omedim penehem kelappe hahekol, veim hem shenayim gedolim o yoter qore lahem hachazzan "kohanim", veim kohen echad bilbad- eno qore lo ella hu lebaddo matchil bibraka:

clarification.explanation: The raising of hands need not take place specifically in a location that has a Torah scroll; rather, in any place where people pray, there is a raising of hands. When they go up to the duchan they stand facing the Ark. If there are two or more kohanim, the chazzan calls out to them "Kohanim"; but if there is only a single kohen, he is not called out to - rather, he begins the blessing on his own.
takeaways: The raising of hands takes place in any place of prayer, even without a Torah scroll.
For two kohanim or more, the chazzan calls out "Kohanim"; for a single kohen he does not, and the kohen begins on his own.

paragraphs: Yagbihu yedehem lemala mikkitpehem sheyyihyu yedehem keneged rosham mammash ukemo shekkatab beshaar hakkavvanot, veayyen "torat chakam" dap qng ammud b vqnd ammud  beinyan zeh. umagbihin yad hayyemanit qetzat lemala mehassemalit, kede lehagbir middat rachamim al middat haddin, uposhetin yedehem, vecholeqin etzbeotehem laasot chamishsha avirim, ben shene etzbaot lishne etzbaot avir echad, uben etzba legudal, uben gudal legodel veyihyeh tok kappehem keneged haaretz, vaachore yedehem keneged hashshamayim vekol zeh kepi mah shekkatab maran za"l beshulchano hattahor, abal bazzohar haqqadosh parashat naso dap qmv katub dela yetachberun etzbaan da bada, bedin deyitbarrekun kitren qaddishin kol chad vechad bilchodohi, vekatab "miqdash melek" dezeh hepek hashshulchan aruk, dekan qaamar shekkol haetzbaot yihyu meporadot zo mizzo, veken katab "aspaqlarya hammeira" al zohar haqqadosh, veshaalti leharab haggaon hechasid morenu harab eliyyahu minni nr"v lehodieni minhag hachasidim b"bet el" ykb"tz birushalayim t"v, vekatab li: baddabar hazzeh en berera yesh osim kemo shekkatab bazzohar haqqadosh, veyesh osim kemo shekkatab maran za"l, ubedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l lo nimtza galuy ledabar zeh, upoh irenu y" nohagim laasot chamishsha avirim, veyesh qetzat nohagim laasot kepi zohar haqqadosh, veod sheiltiv lehodieni minhag hachasidim b"bet el" ykb"tz im hakkohanim etzbeotehem zequpim kemo netilat yadayim, veheshib sheggam bazeh lo yesh hekker, yesh osin kak veyesh osin kak:

clarification.explanation: The kohanim raise their hands above their shoulders, exactly level with their heads, and raise the right hand slightly above the left in order to strengthen mercy over judgment. They spread their hands and separate their fingers into five airy gaps (one gap between each pair of fingers, one between the finger and thumb, and one between the two thumbs), with the palms facing the ground and the backs of the hands facing the heavens, following Maran's view. But the Zohar states that the fingers should not touch one another at all, so that each finger stands independently - a departure from the words of the Shulchan Aruch. Rabbi Eliyahu Mani testified that there is no decisive custom on this in Beit El: some follow the Zohar and some follow Maran; in Baghdad the practice was to make five gaps, with some following the Zohar. And likewise, whether the fingers should be held upright, there is no clear ruling either.
takeaways: The hands are raised level with the head, with the right hand slightly above the left to strengthen mercy.
There is a dispute between the Shulchan Aruch (five gaps) and the Zohar (each finger separate); in Baghdad the practice follows Maran.

paragraphs: Keshemmazkirin hashshem bebirkat kohanim yaanu hatztzibbur "baruk hu ubaruk shemo" vekannizkar bapposeqim, veap al gab deikka dela sebira lehu haki, hamminhag pashut laanot veken hamminhag pashut beir haqqodesh tvb"b veen leshannot, veachar gemar kol pasuq onim hatztzibbur amen, veen onim amen ad shettikleh beraka mippi hakkohanim, abal hsh"tz eno oneh amen achar beraka shel kohanim, vaapillu achar birkat "lebarek et ammo yisrael beahaba" lo yaaneh hsh"tz amen. vaapillu demubtach lo shello yitbalbel:

clarification.explanation: When the kohanim mention the Name of God in the blessing, the congregation answers "Baruch Hu U'varuch Shemo," and this is the widespread custom, not to be changed. After the conclusion of each verse the congregation answers "amen," and they do not answer until the blessing is finished from the mouths of the kohanim. But the chazzan does not answer amen after the kohanim's blessing at all, and even after "to bless His people Israel with love" he shall not answer, even if he is assured he would not become confused in his prayer.
takeaways: The congregation answers "Baruch Hu U'varuch Shemo" at the mention of the Name, and "amen" at the end of each verse.
The chazzan does not answer amen after the kohanim's blessing at all.

paragraphs: Kesheolim laddukan yihyeh penehem kelappe hahekol vaachorehem kelappe haam, ubeod achorehem kelappe haam matchilim lebarek "asher qiddeshanu biqdushshato shel aharon vetzivvanu lebarek et ammo yisrael", machazirim penehem kelappe haam umesayyemim "beahaba", kede sheyyihyeh siyyum habberaka kelappe haam, ukeshemmatchil shelicha tzibbur "sim shalom" az machazirin penehem kelappe hahekol, velo yachaziru penehem qodem, veaz omerim "ribbon haolamim asinu mah sheggazarta alenu aseh atta mah shehibtachtanu hashqipa mimmeon qadeshka min hashshamayim ubarek et ammeka yisrael" veen mesayyemin happasuq hazzeh, veken hamminhag beir haqqodesh tvbb" sheomerim ad kan veen mesayyemin happasuq veyaariku bitpilla zo ad sheyyesayyem hashlicha tzibbur "sim shalom" kede sheyyaanu hatztzibbur amen al shenehem, uberosh hashshana veyom hakkippurim shemmaarikin lo yatchilu lomar "ribbon" ad lebassop kede sheyyesayyemu im haqqahal beyachad, veen hakkohanim rashshain lehachzir penehem ad sheyyatchil shelicha tzibbur "sim shalom", veen rashshain lakop etzbeotehem ad sheyyachzeru penehem veen rashshain laaqor mishsham ad sheyyaanu hatztzibbur amen achar birkat "sim shalom", ukeshemmechazirin penehem ben battechilla ben bassop la yechazzeru ella derek yamin:

clarification.explanation: When they go up to the duchan their faces are toward the Ark and their backs toward the people. While their backs are to the people, they begin the blessing "Who has sanctified us with the sanctity of Aaron and commanded us to bless His people Israel," and at the word "be'ahavah" they turn their faces toward the people, so that the conclusion of the blessing faces the people. When the chazzan begins "Sim Shalom" they turn their faces toward the Ark, and not before, and then say the request "Master of the worlds, we have done what You decreed upon us; do You [now] what You have promised us," up to "and bless Your people Israel," without completing the verse, and they prolong it until the chazzan concludes "Sim Shalom," so that the congregation answers amen upon both. On Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, when it is prolonged, they should not begin "Ribon" until the end, so as to conclude together with the congregation. The kohanim may not turn their faces back until the chazzan begins "Sim Shalom"; they may not bend their fingers until after turning their faces back; and they may not leave their place until the congregation answers amen after the blessing "Sim Shalom." And every turning of the face shall be by way of the right.
takeaways: They open the blessing with their backs to the people, and turn to face the people at "be'ahavah."

At "Sim Shalom" they face the Ark and say "Ribon HaOlamim"; they bend their fingers only after turning back, and do not step down from the duchan until the congregation answers amen after "Sim Shalom"; every turn is made to the right.

paragraphs: En qore hashlicha tzibbur "kohanim" ella ad sheyyikleh amen shel birkat "naeh lehodot" mippi hatztzibbur, veen hakkohanim rashshain lehatchil birkat "asher qiddeshanu" ad sheyyikleh dibbur qeriat "kohanim" mippi haqqore, veen rashshain lehatchil "yebarekka" ad sheyyikleh amen mippi kol hatztzibbur achar "beahaba", veen rashshain lehatchil beshum teba min birkat kohanim ad shettikleh hatteba mippi hammiqra, veen hatztzibbur onin amen ad shettikleh habberaka mippi hakkohanim:

clarification.explanation: The chazzan does not call out "Kohanim" until the congregation's answer of "amen" to the blessing "U'lecha na'eh lehodot" has finished. The kohanim may not begin "Who has sanctified us" until the chazzan's calling of "Kohanim" has finished, and they do not begin "yevarechecha" until the entire congregation's "amen" after "be'ahavah" has finished. And regarding every word: the kohanim do not begin a word until the caller has finished it, and the congregation does not answer "amen" until the blessing has finished from the mouths of the kohanim.
takeaways: The order must be kept: each stage begins only after the previous one has fully ended.
The kohanim do not get ahead of the one calling out, and the congregation does not get ahead of the kohanim.

paragraphs: Nakon lehishtaddel shello yihyeh kohen shelicha tzibbur beshacharit umusap, veim haya hashlicha tzibbur kohen im yesh kohanim acherim sham lo yissa kappayv, veim en sham kohen ella hu umubtach lo sheyyachazor litpillato belo terup haddaat hare zeh nose kappayv, kede shello titbattel nesiut kappayim meotah tepilla, ketzad yaaseh? yaaqor raglayv baaboda, veyomar ad "uleka naeh lehodot" veyaaleh laddukan vibarek birkat kohanim, veim hatztzibbur kullam lepanayv yebarek otam bimqomo veyiqra lo acher et birkat kohanim, veachar kak yesayyem "sim shalom", vekol heka deikka kohanim acherim deamerinan shehashlicha tzibbur lo yissa kappayv tzarik sheyyihyeh omed bimqomo veshoteq, veadam acher yaamod etzlo veyiqra et hakkohanim, vehashshalicha tzibbur shoteq ad hatchalat "sim shalom":

clarification.explanation: It is proper to make an effort that the chazzan for Shacharit and Musaf not be a kohen. If the chazzan was a kohen and there are other kohanim present, he shall not raise his hands. And if there is no other kohen present besides him, and he is assured he will return to his prayer without becoming confused, he does raise his hands so that the blessing not be omitted: he uproots his feet at [the blessing of] "Retzeh"/Avodah, says [the prayer] up to "U'lecha na'eh lehodot," goes up to the duchan and blesses; and if the whole congregation is ahead of him he blesses in his place, and someone else calls out the blessing for him, after which he concludes "Sim Shalom." And wherever there are other kohanim present and the chazzan should not raise his hands, he stands in his place and remains silent, while another person stands beside him and calls out to the kohanim, and the chazzan remains silent until the beginning of "Sim Shalom."
takeaways: It is preferable that the chazzan not be a kohen; and if there are other kohanim present, the chazzan does not raise his hands.
If there is no other kohen, the chazzan does raise his hands, provided he is assured he will return to his prayer without becoming confused.

paragraphs: Beshaa shehakkohanim mebarekim et haam yihyu pene haam keneged hakkohanim velo yabbitu bakkohanim velo beshum dabar acher, veyihyu enehem segurot velo yassichu datam bidbarim acherim, veyihyu kemo sheomedim battepilla, veyitkavvenu libraka, veam sheachore hakkohanim enam biklal habberaka, veken haomedim bitzdadim kol sheen omedim baavir asher mippenehem veelak enam biklal habberaka, abal otam haomedim bitzdadim shel haavir shellipnehem hare ellu biklal habberaka, dela baenan lipnehem mammash ki im al tzad hayyoter tob heka deepshar vekannizkar b"chesed laalapim", veim echad niknas lebet hakkeneset lebaqqesh ezeh dabar, o ober orach mimmaqom lemaqom umatza hakkohanim mebarekin birkat kohanim, yaamod veyishma birkat kohanim velo yatza ad sheyyesayyemu birkat kohanim, veim hu kohen ukebar nasa kappayv beoto hayyom, uba lebet hakkeneset zo umatza tzibbur shello higgiu lebirkat kohanim, yakol lissa kappayv paam acheret:

clarification.explanation: At the time the kohanim bless, the faces of the people must be toward the kohanim, and they shall not look at the kohanim or at anything else, but shall stand with their eyes closed with intent, as in prayer. Those standing behind the kohanim are not included in the blessing, nor those standing to the sides who are not within the space in front of the kohanim; but those standing to the sides of the space in front of them are included in the blessing, since it is not required that they stand exactly opposite them. Someone who enters the synagogue for some purpose, or a traveler passing through, who finds the kohanim blessing, shall stand and listen and not leave until they finish. And a kohen who has already raised his hands that day and comes to another synagogue and finds a congregation that has not yet reached Birkat Kohanim may raise his hands again.
takeaways: The congregation stands facing the kohanim with closed eyes and intent, without looking at them.
Those standing behind are not included in the blessing; a kohen may raise his hands again in another synagogue.

paragraphs: Kohen shello hitpallel adayin umatza tzibbur mitpallelin: im en hashshaa oberet nose kappayv veen hattepilla meakkabto, veim ameru lo "aleh" tzarik laalot apillu hashshaa oberet lo, dinsiut kappayim deorayeta utepilla derabbanan:

clarification.explanation: A kohen who has not yet prayed and finds a congregation praying: if the time [for prayer] is not passing, he raises his hands, and his prayer does not hold him back. And if they told him "go up," he must go up even if the time is passing for him, since the raising of hands is from the Torah while prayer is rabbinic.
takeaways: A kohen who has not yet prayed raises his hands if the time is not passing.
If he is told "go up," he must, since the raising of hands is a Torah commandment while prayer is rabbinic.

paragraphs: Kohen haqqore qeriat shema vehirgish dehashshalicha tzibbur mukan lehaggia lebirkat kohanim, yemaher lesayyem haqriat shema sheyyiqra bah gam bederek hilluko laalot kede sheyyesayyem otah qodem sheyyatchil lebarek, veim hirgish bazeh beodo bebirkot qeriat shema, yamtin sham beben happeraqim velo yatchil biqriat shema ad sheyyebarek birkat kohanim. veim lo hirgish ella ad shehitchil shelicha tzibbur b"retzeh" vehu kebar hitchil biqriat shema, vehu kebad peh shei epshar lemaher lesayyem haqriat shema qodem sheyyebarek, hinneh zeh yaaqor raglayv baaboda, visayyem happarasha shehu omed bah vibarek birkat kohanim ben happeraqim shel qeriat shema, veachar birkat kohanim yesayyem haqriat shema, abal im lo hirgish baaboda, velo aqar raglayv qodem shessiyyem shelicha tzibbur birkat aboda eno oleh laddukan lebarek, ukemo shekkatabti leel dekol shello aqar raglayv baaboda eno oleh laddukan, vekaasher heeleti kol zeh besipre haq' "rab pealim" besiyyata dishmayya. veim hakkohen omed bitpilla, katabti sham besipre haq' "rab pealim" daapillu lisbarat ha"magen abraham" udeimmeh disbira lehu poseq, zeh eno ella im ken ameru lo laalot, vetzarik sheyyomru lo kesheomer hashlicha tzibbur "retzeh", ak beemet yesh choleqim al ha"magen abraham" usebira lehu deeno poseq im omed hattepilla, kedin qaddish uqedushsha, vaapillu lisbarat hassoberim deim hakkohen hammitpallel siyyem "uleka naeh lehodot" hinneh zeh nose kappayv sham, im kol zeh kevan dela aqar raglo baaboda eno oleh, ubevadday dela aqar raglayv kevan dehaya asuq bitpillato, ubevadday dela yomru lo laalot kevan deroin oto oseq bitpilla, vekevan dela ameru lo laalot az gam lisbarat harab mahara"m minetz za"l siman yb lo yissa kappayv:

clarification.explanation: A kohen reciting the Shema who senses that the chazzan is close to Birkat Kohanim shall hurry to finish the Shema, even while walking up, in order to finish before the blessing. If he sensed this while still in the blessings surrounding the Shema, he shall wait at a break between the sections and not begin the Shema itself until after he has blessed Birkat Kohanim. And if he did not sense it until "Retzeh" and had already begun the Shema, and is slow of speech so that he cannot hurry to finish before the blessing - he shall uproot his feet at "Retzeh," finish the passage he is in, and bless between the sections of the Shema, and afterward finish the Shema. But if he did not uproot his feet before the chazzan finished the blessing of "Avodah," he does not go up to the duchan at all. And a kohen standing in the [silent] Amidah itself does not go up unless he was explicitly told to go up at the time of "Retzeh" - and in practice there are those who disagree even with that, and since he did not uproot his feet during Avodah, he does not go up.
takeaways: A kohen reciting the Shema should hurry or wait between sections in order to bless at the proper point.
The principle: whoever did not uproot his feet at "Retzeh" does not go up to the duchan.

paragraphs: Kohen abal yotze mibbet hakkeneset beshaa sheqqore kohanim, veachar shibat yeme abelut yissa kappayv, veyesh omerim daapillu betok shiba yissa kappayv vealayv tabo birkat tob, ubeir haqqodesh yerushalim tvb"b nahagu laasot nesiut kappayim bebet haabel, veken nahagu mechadash poh irenu bagdad y", veraq hakkohanim shehem abelim lo nahagu lissa kappayim, vetzarik lehazhiram shello yaamdu sham, ella yikkanesu qodem "ratza" tok cheder acher shebbabbayit, veayyen b"shalme tzibbur" veayyen mah shekkatab harab hammaggihha b"chesed laalapim" beshem harab mh"r chayyim pineso za"l yeuyyan sham, ubiqhal chasidim "bet el" ykb"tz nohagim laasot nesiut kappayim betisha beab beshacharit, upoh irenu y" lo nahagu betisha beab ken, ella raq bemincha davqa osin nesiut kappayim, velo shinniti minhagam bazeh betisha beab, mittaam hakkamus itti:

clarification.explanation: A mourning kohen leaves the synagogue at the time "Kohanim" is called, and after the seven days of mourning he raises his hands; and some say that even during the seven days he raises his hands, to his blessing. In Jerusalem the custom is to perform the raising of hands in the house of mourning, and this has become the new custom in Baghdad as well - except that the mourning kohanim themselves did not raise their hands, and one must warn them not to stand there but to enter another room before "Retzeh." In Beit El they practice raising hands on the ninth of Av at Shacharit, but in Baghdad they did not practice this at Shacharit, only at Mincha of the ninth of Av, and our teacher did not change their custom in this matter for a reason kept within him.
takeaways: A mourning kohen does not raise his hands during the seven days, and leaves at the time of the calling.
In Baghdad they raise hands on the ninth of Av only at Mincha, not at Shacharit.

paragraphs: En osin nesiut kappayim bemincha ella raq betaanit tzibbur sheddarkam lehitacher lehitpallel kemo zeman tepillat neila shel yom hakkippurim, ubitshubati besipri haq' "rab pealim" heeleti lehorot lahem lekattechilla laasot nesiut kappayim betaanit tzibbur arbaim deqim qodem qeriat hmgr"b (haereb) shehu chatzi shaa qodem sheqiat hachamma, ki poh irenu hachamma shoqaat asara daqqim qodem qeriat hmgr"b, mihu otam sheosim qodem shiur hannizkar en limchot beyadam sheyyesh lahem al mah sheyyismoku:

clarification.explanation: The raising of hands is not performed at Mincha, except on a public fast day when it is customary to pray late, at a time similar to the Ne'ilah prayer of Yom Kippur. Our teacher ruled that as the preferred practice, the raising of hands should be performed on a public fast day about forty minutes before the calling of the evening prayer - a point that is about half an hour before sunset, since in Baghdad the sun sets about ten minutes before that calling. Those who perform it somewhat before this measure should not be protested against, since they have grounds to rely on.
takeaways: The raising of hands at Mincha occurs only on a public fast day, at the late hour similar to Ne'ilah.
The proper time: about half an hour before sunset (in Baghdad, about forty minutes before the calling of the evening prayer).

paragraphs: Halakot ellu shayyakim lepurim darke ledaresham bzh"y beshabbat zakur asher al harob yizdammen beparashat tetzavveh veqishshur shellahem yihyeh betok hadderasha kepi mah sheyyizdammen bekol shana veshana bzh"y:

clarification.explanation: These halachot pertain to Purim, and our teacher's practice was to expound them on Shabbat Zachor, which for the most part falls at the time of Parashat Tetzaveh, and their connection to the parasha is made within the sermon as it happens to occur each year.
takeaways: The halachot of Purim are expounded on Shabbat Zachor, which usually falls at the time of Parashat Tetzaveh.

paragraphs: Hakkol chayyabin bemiqra megilla anashim venashim ak hannashim "p sheyyodein liqrot yishmeu min haanashim veken hamminhag bh"q tvb"b shemmeolam lo nishma shehaishsha qarea megilla velaken kol adam "p sheqqara hammegilla bebet hakkeneset yiqraenna bebeto bishbil ishto shello shamea bebet hakkeneset ubishbil habbetulot ushear nashim umesharetim shebbabbayit veim qeraah bebet hakkeneset vechozer veqore lannashim lo yebarek bishbilam vegam hem lo yebareku:

clarification.explanation: All are obligated in the reading of the Megillah, men and women. But the women, even though they know how to read, shall listen from the men, and so is the custom - it has never been heard that a woman read the Megillah. Therefore, every man, even though he read the Megillah in the synagogue, shall read it again at home for his wife who did not hear it in the synagogue, and for the unmarried girls, the other women, and the household servants. And if he already read in the synagogue and reads again for the women, he shall not make the blessing on their behalf, nor shall they make the blessing themselves.
takeaways: Women are obligated in the Megillah but hear it from the men and do not read it themselves.
One who reads again at home for the women after having heard it in the synagogue does not make the blessing.

paragraphs: Im haya haqqore cheresh o shoteh o qatan hashshomea mimmennu lo yatza y"ch vetzarik lachazor veliqrotah bibraka mihu im shamea mecheresh yachazor veyiqraenna belo beraka mishshum deikka ds"l shomea mecheresh yatza veim shamea miqqatan shehiggia lechinnuk yachzor veyiqraenna belo beraka deikka rabbim ds"l qatan shehiggia lechinnuk motzi et haggadol y"ch veken name im shamea mehaishsha yachzor veyiqraenna belo beraka:

clarification.explanation: If the reader was deaf-mute [in the sense of one lacking full faculties], mentally incompetent, or a minor [who has not reached the age of training], one who hears from him has not fulfilled the obligation at all and must go back and read with a blessing. But if one heard from a person who can speak but not hear, he shall go back and read without a blessing, since some hold that hearing from such a person fulfills the obligation. Likewise, if one heard from a minor who has reached the age of training, he shall go back and read without a blessing, since many hold that such a minor can fulfill the obligation even for an adult. And likewise, if one heard from a woman, he shall go back and read without a blessing.
takeaways: One who hears from someone mentally incompetent, or a minor below the age of training, has not fulfilled the obligation at all and reads again with a blessing; one who hears from a person who can speak but not hear, from a minor who has reached the age of training, or from a woman, reads again without a blessing, out of doubt.
Out of doubt, one does not bless again, since there are lenient views in all these cases.

paragraphs: Qeraah mitnamnem hoil velo nirdam beshena yatza abal hashshomea im mitnamnem lo yatza vetzarik lehizzaher bd"z shehu matzuy tamid deellu hashshomeim yitnamnemu, ulekattechilla im rau et haqqore sheqqara ezeh pesuqim mitnamnem makrichin oto sheyyachazor veyiqraenna, dela amerinan qeraah mitnamnem yatza ella bediabad heka desiyyem qeriat hammegilla kullah:

clarification.explanation: One who read the Megillah while drowsy, since he did not fall into a deep sleep, has fulfilled the obligation. But one who listens while drowsy has not fulfilled the obligation, and one must be careful about this, since it commonly happens that listeners become drowsy. As the preferred practice, if it was observed that the reader read some verses while drowsy, he is required to go back and read it again, since the ruling that one who read while drowsy has fulfilled the obligation applies only after the fact, once he has completed reading the entire Megillah.
takeaways: A drowsy reader has fulfilled the obligation after the fact, but a drowsy listener has not.
As the preferred practice, a reader who dozed off partway through is required to start over.

paragraphs: Haqqore et hammegilla tzarik lebarek habberakot meummad ben battechilla ben bassop apillu hu qoreah yachid bebeto, abal qeriatah enah tzerika meummad, veraq hsh"tz qoreah meummad mippene kebod hatztzibbur, vetzarik lihyot poshet otah kullah veaach"k mebarek habberakot meummad, mihu meachar deposhet umebarek beodo omed, tzarik sheyyihyeh lepanayv bima o kisse shettanucha alayv hammegilla velo tihyeh nigreret baaretz:

clarification.explanation: One who reads the Megillah makes the blessings while standing, at the beginning and at the end, even if reading it alone at home. But the reading itself does not require standing, and only the prayer leader reads it standing, out of respect for the congregation. He must unroll the entire Megillah before the blessing, and since he unrolls it and blesses while standing, he must have before him a table or chair for the Megillah to rest on, so that it does not drag on the ground.
takeaways: The blessings on the Megillah are made standing, at the beginning and the end, even by an individual.
The entire Megillah is unrolled before the blessing, and rested on a table so it does not drag on the ground.

paragraphs: Mi sheshshakach velo berek shehecheyanu, im nizkar achar shehitchil yebarek bammaqom shennizkar, vbsh"q mqbtzyl heeleti deim lo nizkar ad achar shekkebar qara gam pasuq aseret bene haman, "p sheadayin lo gamar hammegilla lo yebarek shehecheyanu sham bammaqom shennizkar:

clarification.explanation: One who forgot to recite the blessing of "Shehecheyanu" before the reading, if he remembers after having begun, shall recite it at the point where he remembers. But if he did not remember until after he has already read the verse of the ten sons of Haman, even though he has not yet finished the Megillah, he shall no longer recite "Shehecheyanu" there.
takeaways: One who forgot "Shehecheyanu" and remembers partway through the reading recites it at that point.
If he has passed the verse of the ten sons of Haman, he no longer recites it.

paragraphs: Im hishmit haqqore millot biqriato apillu shehem tebot sheen mapsidin inyan haqqeria lo yatza y"ch, umi sheyyesh beyado megilla sheenah keshera yishma mishshelicha tzibbur veyishtoq:

clarification.explanation: If the reader omitted words in his reading, even words that do not change the meaning of the matter, he has not fulfilled the obligation. And one who has an invalid Megillah in his possession shall not read from it, but shall listen to the chazzan and remain silent.
takeaways: Omitting words, even ones not essential to the meaning, invalidates the fulfillment of the obligation.
One without a valid Megillah listens to the chazzan and remains silent.

paragraphs: Nohagin lomar d' pesuqim shel geulla bqv"r, vehem ish yehudi veku', ballayla hahu veku', umareddekay yatza veku', layyehudim hayeta ora veku', ukesheomer pasuq ballayla hahu beqol ram veniggun yesayyem tebat hammelek bqv"r veniggun beyoter, veyesh nohagim lor g"k pasuq ki mareddekay hayyehudi veku' upoh irenu lo nahagu bepasuq zeh:

clarification.explanation: It is customary to say four verses of redemption aloud: "Ish Yehudi," "BaLailah HaHu," "U'Mordechai Yatza," "LaYehudim Haytah Orah." And when saying "BaLailah HaHu" aloud with melody, one prolongs the word "HaMelech" in particular. Some are accustomed to also say the verse "Ki Mordechai HaYehudi" aloud, but in Baghdad they were not accustomed to do so with this verse.
takeaways: Four verses of redemption are said aloud, headed by "Ish Yehudi."
In "BaLailah HaHu" the word "HaMelech" is prolonged.

paragraphs: Tzarik lomar mittechillat chamesh meot ish veet parshandata veku' aseret binshima achat, veyaarik beva"v shel vayzata, vehamminhag lehakkot beraglayv al haqqarqa kesheomerim shemot aseret bene haman, veyesh nohagim lehakkot beyadam al haqqarqa veen zeh minhag yapeh, ella rauy lehakkot besandalim shebberaglehem:

clarification.explanation: The names of the ten sons of Haman, from "Chamesh Me'ot Ish" and "Ve'et Parshandata" through "Aseret," must be said in a single breath, and one prolongs the vav of "VeVaizata." The custom is to stamp with the feet on the floor when saying the names of the ten sons of Haman. Some are accustomed to strike with the hand on the floor, but this is not a becoming custom - rather it is proper to stamp with the sandals on one's feet.
takeaways: The names of the ten sons of Haman are said in a single breath, with a prolongation of the vav of "VeVaizata."
One stamps with the feet (in sandals), not with the hand.

paragraphs: Tzarik lehizzaher liqrot tebat "veet" hannizkarim baaseret bene haman mittok hammegilla, ki yesh toim mechamat hammehirut shelal neshima achat liqrot kol tebot shel veet hannaz' b"p, lekak tzarik lehasim leb al zot lehizzaher, ukesheomer "vayyiqqar" yasim yadayv al hattepillin vinashsheq, ukesheorem et iggeret happurim yenanea hammegilla betebat iggeret:

clarification.explanation: One must be careful to read the words "ve'et" that appear before the ten sons of Haman directly from the Megillah itself, since some err, out of haste, and read all the instances of "ve'et" from memory; therefore one must pay attention to this. When saying "vayikar," one places his hands on the tefillin and kisses them, and when saying "the letter of Purim," one shakes the Megillah at the word "iggeret" (letter).
takeaways: The words "ve'et" are read from the text, not from memory.
Customs: kissing the tefillin at "vayikar," and shaking the Megillah at "iggeret."

paragraphs: Katab haggaon yaabe"tz za"l al abiv haggaon za"l shehaya makkeh beraglo vetopeach besandalo keshemmazkir shem hamman biqriat hammegilla "sh, vaani ragil lehakkot baregalim beshem haman harishon hakkatub bappasuq achar haddebarim haelleh giddal hammelek achashverosh et haman ben hammedata haagagi, vegam od shem haman haacharon bappasuq ki haman ben hammedata haagagi tzorer kol hayyehudim chashab veku':

clarification.explanation: The Gaon Ya'avetz wrote of his father that he would stamp with his foot and strike with his sandal at every mention of the name "Haman" during the reading of the Megillah. Our teacher was accustomed to strike with his feet only at the first mention of "Haman," in the verse "After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hamedatha the Agagite," and at the last mention of "Haman," in the verse "For Haman the son of Hamedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted, etc."
takeaways: Some struck at every mention of the name "Haman."
Our teacher was accustomed to strike only at the first and the last mention of "Haman" in the Megillah.

paragraphs: Asur leekol qodem qeriat hammegilla, veim yesh leadam megilla keshera sheqqore bah leatzmo bebet hakkeneset beet shhsh"tz qore sham bishbil hatztzibbur, vezeh eno rotzeh latzet bibraka shel sh"tz ella yirtzeh lebarek leatzmo rashshay, ak yebarek belachash vekaasher heeleti bsh"q rab pealim bs"d:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to eat before the reading of the Megillah. And one who has a valid Megillah and reads it for himself in the synagogue while the chazzan is reading for the congregation, and does not wish to fulfill his obligation through the chazzan's blessing but wishes to bless for himself, is permitted to do so, but shall make the blessing quietly.
takeaways: It is forbidden to eat before the reading of the Megillah.
One who reads from his own Megillah may bless for himself, but quietly.

paragraphs: Tob sheyyaamdu shene anashim etzel hsh"tz miyyamin umissemol, veyomar hsh"tz qodem habberaka birshut mori verabbotay vibarek veyiqra, uminhag irenu sheyyaamdu haqqahal beet habberaka battechilla ubassop, vekol adam tzarik sheyyiglol veaach"k yebarek beraka acharona, veyizzaher shello yebarek beet shehu golel hammegilla:

clarification.explanation: It is good that two people stand beside the chazzan, to his right and to his left, and the chazzan says before the blessing, "With the permission of my teachers and masters," and then blesses and reads. The custom of Baghdad is that the congregation stands during the blessing, at the beginning and at the end. Every person rolls up the Megillah and only afterward recites the concluding blessing, and he must be careful not to recite the blessing while still rolling it.
takeaways: Two people stand beside the chazzan, and he opens with "With the permission of my teachers and masters."
One rolls up the Megillah before the concluding blessing, and does not bless while rolling it.

paragraphs: Haqqore yachid yebarek gam beraka acharona shel hammegilla vknz' bebirke yosep veayyen ml"ch si' l" ot q"ch y"sh, veken hamminhag poh irenu veken rauy linhog bk"m, velo yeabbed hayyachid beraka yeqara zo:

clarification.explanation: One who reads the Megillah alone also recites the blessing that follows the Megillah, and so is the custom in Baghdad, and so it is fitting to practice everywhere, so that the individual not lose out on this precious blessing.
takeaways: Even one who reads alone recites the blessing that follows the Megillah.
It is fitting that the individual not forgo this blessing.

paragraphs: Omerim al hannissim bitpilla vbhm"z beyom y"d davqa, abal lo beyom t"v, vaapillu maqom sheqqorin hammegilla bt"v mishshum sapeq im hayeta muqqepet choma mimot yehoshua k"z lo yomru al hannissim bitpilla vbhm"z mippene chashash hepseq, veken, meporash beshaar hakkavvanot, upoh irenu bagdad y" minhagam liqrot hammegilla by"d bibraka abal bt"v qorin otah belo beraka kelal, uberaka acharona omerim otah beli shem umalkut, uminhagam liqrot bt"v bs"t beparashat vayyabo amaleq, vehattaam deir bagdad yesh bah sapeq im hayeta muqqepet choma mimot yehoshua o lav, velaken qorin bt"v et hammegilla belo beraka, umiqqadmat dena haya hamminhag poh irenu lomar al hannissim beyom t"v bitpilla vbbhm"z, ak hrh"g t"r mor zeqeni rabbenu mosheh chayyim zlh"h bittel hamminhag shel amirat al hannissim mishshum chashash pesaq, abal qeriat s"t lo ratza lebattel deen kan chashash beraka lebattala, velaken atta en omerim al hannissim poh ayarenu bagdad ella raq beyom y"d bilbad, veim shakach velo amar en machazirim oto, ella debitpilla omer achar elohay netzor nodeh leka Adonai v" al hannissim veku', vbbhm"z yomar achar siyyum habberakot harachaman hu yaaseh lanu nissim keshem sheasa laabotenu bayyamim hahem bzh"z ubime mareddekay veku':

clarification.explanation: "Al HaNisim" is said in the prayer and Grace after Meals specifically on the fourteenth, not on the fifteenth. Even in a place that reads the Megillah on the fifteenth out of doubt whether it was walled from the days of Joshua, they do not say "Al HaNisim" on the fifteenth out of concern for improper interruption in prayer. In Baghdad they read the Megillah on the fourteenth with a blessing, and on the fifteenth without any blessing at all (and the concluding blessing without mentioning God's Name and Sovereignty), and they read on the fifteenth from a Torah scroll the portion "Vayavo Amalek," because there is doubt whether Baghdad was walled. Formerly they also said "Al HaNisim" on the fifteenth, but our teacher's grandfather abolished this custom out of concern for interruption, though he did not abolish the Torah reading, since there is no concern of a wasted blessing there. One who forgot to say "Al HaNisim" is not required to repeat the prayer, but says it after "Elohai Netzor" in the Amidah, and in Grace after Meals in the "HaRachaman" formula.
takeaways: "Al HaNisim" is said only on the fourteenth, even in places that read on the fifteenth out of doubt.
In Baghdad the Megillah is read on the fifteenth without a blessing and from a Torah scroll, out of doubt whether the city was walled.

paragraphs: Chayyab kol adam litten shette mattanot lishne aniyyim lepachot, vekol hammarbeh baruk yihyeh, vehashshiur hu im noten okel tzarik sheyyihyeh bo g' betzim shehem arbaa vachamishsha drh"m, veim maot shiur sheyyiqneh shelosha betzim mippat, vaapillu ani hammitparnes mitztzedaqa chayyab bemattanot laebyonim vhpr"ch potero, vekatub beseper tora lishmah sheyyukal ebyon echad litten leebyon chabero vezeh g"k chozer venoten lachabero:

clarification.explanation: Every person is obligated to give at least two gifts to two poor people, and whoever gives more is praiseworthy. The measure: if giving food, it should be about three eggs' worth (about four or five dirhams); if giving money, enough to buy three eggs' worth of bread. Even a poor person who is himself supported by charity is obligated in gifts to the poor (though the Peri Chadash exempts him). And it is written in the book Torah LiShmah that one poor person can give his gift to his fellow poor person, who in turn gives it again to another.
takeaways: One must give at least two gifts to two poor people, in the measure of about three eggs' worth.
Even a poor person is obligated, and poor people may pass gifts to one another.

paragraphs: Chayyab lishloach kol adam lachabero shene manot dehaynu shene mine okalim vekatub beseper tora lishmah shetztzarik lehannicha kol min bikli echad bp" velo yannicha shenehem bikli echad umishlocha manot tzarik lishloach legadol abal mattanot laebyonim apillu natan leqatan yatza y"ch:

clarification.explanation: Every person is obligated to send to his fellow "two portions," that is, two kinds of food. And it is written in the book Torah LiShmah that one should place each kind in a separate container, and not place both in one container. Mishloach manot must be sent to an adult; but gifts to the poor fulfill the obligation even if given to a minor.
takeaways: Mishloach manot: two kinds of food, each in its own separate container.
Portions are sent to an adult; gifts to the poor may also be given to a minor.

paragraphs: Haishsha chayyebet g"k bemishlocha manot umattanot laebyonim, upoh ayarenu bgd"d sheqqorin hammegilla gam bt"v belo beraka mishshum sapeq muqqepet choma, tzarik leqayyem beyom t"v seuda umishlocha manot umattanot laebyonim echad anashim veechad nashim, veraq en marbin bahem kemo yom y"d:

clarification.explanation: A woman is likewise obligated in mishloach manot and gifts to the poor. In Baghdad, where the Megillah is also read on the fifteenth without a blessing out of doubt whether the city was walled, one must observe on the fifteenth a festive meal, mishloach manot, and gifts to the poor, for men and women alike, only without increasing them as on the fourteenth.
takeaways: A woman is also obligated in mishloach manot and gifts to the poor.
In Baghdad the day's mitzvot, including the meal, are observed on the fifteenth as well, but in a reduced measure.

paragraphs: Abal tok y"b chodesh shel ab o shel em yeqayyem mishlocha manot ak lo yishlach leharbeh bene adam ella yeqayyem hammitzva hazzot beadam echad davqa, velo lo yishlechu acherim kelal:

clarification.explanation: One who is within the twelve months of mourning for his father or mother fulfills mishloach manot, but does not send to many people; rather, he fulfills this commandment with a single person only. And likewise, others shall not send mishloach manot to him at all.
takeaways: A mourner within the twelve months sends mishloach manot to a single person only.
One does not send mishloach manot to a mourner.

paragraphs: Mitzva leharbot bisudat purim, veiqqar hasseuda bayyom, veim asaah ballayla lo yatza y"ch, uminhag yapeh leekol zereonim bepurim zeker laakilat zereonim sheakelu daniyyel vachaberayv veasa lahem hqb"h nes bazeh, velaken poh ayarenu minhagam letaggen mulyayta beqitniyyot ubasar beyachad sheqqorin zeh bearbe smbvs"k:

clarification.explanation: It is a mitzvah to abound in the festive meal of Purim, and the essential meal is during the day; one who holds it at night has not fulfilled the obligation. It is a good custom to eat legumes on Purim, in remembrance of the legumes eaten by Daniel and his companions, for whom a miracle was performed. Therefore in Baghdad the custom is to fry a pastry filled with legumes and meat together, called in Arabic "sambusak."
takeaways: The essential Purim meal is during the day; one who holds it only at night has not fulfilled the obligation.
It is customary to eat legumes, in remembrance of the miracle of Daniel and his companions.

paragraphs: Minhag yapeh liktob amaleq veshem hamman velimchuttam, veqodem simmecham yidros veyakkeh alehem besandalo, velo yimchem beroq shebbepiv ella bemayim mezohamim, veim yesh shekar lepanayv yimchem beshekar vesiman tenu shekar leobed:

clarification.explanation: It is a good custom to write "Amalek" and the name of Haman and to erase them. Before erasing, one tramples and strikes upon them with his sandal, and does not erase them with spittle from his mouth but with dirty (murky) water. And if he has strong drink before him, he erases them with the strong drink, as a hint from the verse "Give strong drink to him who is perishing."
takeaways: It is customary to write "Amalek" and Haman's name and erase them, after trampling them with a sandal.
One erases them with murky water or with strong drink, not with spittle.

paragraphs: En laasot melaka bepurim ben by"d ben bt"v, veen lannashim laasot kibbus vekaddomeh apillu beyom t"v, veen megallechin hayyisreelim apillu im chal yom y"d beereb shabbat:

clarification.explanation: One shall not perform work on Purim, whether on the fourteenth or the fifteenth. Women shall not do laundry and the like, even on the fifteenth day. And Israelites do not get haircuts, even if the fourteenth falls on a Friday.
takeaways: Work is not performed on Purim, on either the fourteenth or the fifteenth.
Haircuts are not given, even when the fourteenth falls on Friday.

paragraphs: Yilbeshu bepurim bigde shabbat o begadim acherim shehem chashubim, velo yilbeshu bigde chol, zeh hayyom asa Adonai nagila venismecha bo:

clarification.explanation: On Purim one wears Shabbat clothing or other fine garments, and does not wear weekday clothing, as it is written: "This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it."
takeaways: On Purim one wears Shabbat clothing or fine garments, not weekday clothing.
